text:
The Models
We use linear models for amplitude and decay rate as dependent variables, with group as the independent factor, checking fit in Figure 1.

Show the code
# Fit the models
model6b_amp_lm <- lm(amplitude ~ group, data=dfms$dfm_6b)
model6b_k_lm <- lm(decayrate ~ group, data=dfms$dfm_6b)

# Check model fit
performance::check_model(model6b_amp_lm)
performance::check_model(model6b_k_lm)












(a) amplitude ~ group











(b) decayrate ~ group







Figure 1: Diagnostic plots for linear model fits of amplitude ~ group and decayrate ~ group. The heteroscadicity spline is odd, but the datapoints are not particularly concerning. There is some evidence of non-normality of residuals in the decay rate constant data, but nothing especially concerning.



As the model fit is acceptable, we estimate contrasts in Table 2.


Show the code
EMM <- emmeans::emmeans(model6b_amp_lm, ~ group)
confint(emmeans::contrast(EMM, "pairwise", adjust="sidak")) |>
  kableExtra::kbl(digits=3) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("hover", "responsive")

title: Figure 6b: WT NeRh50 maximum amplitudes and decay rate constants after a 200 mM ammonium pulse in proteoliposomes containing NeRh50 at LPR10, at four pH conditions
text:
The Figures
We plot the data, indicating P-values for the contrasts in Figure 2.

Show the code
# Get p-values, accounting for heteroscedasticity and multiple testing
# Also generate group1 and group2 columns
EMM_amp <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model6b_amp_lm, ~ group),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=2.5) |>
  rstatix::add_significance()

EMM_k <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model6b_k_lm, ~ group),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=70) |>
  rstatix::add_significance()

p6b_amp <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfms$dfm_6b, 
                           ggplot2::aes(x=group, y=amplitude, color=group)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Maximum amplitude (nA)") +
  ggplot2::ylim(0, 3.5) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(EMM_amp,
                             label="p = {scales::pvalue(p.value)}",
                             size=3, step.increase=0.1)

p6b_k <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfms$dfm_6b, 
                         ggplot2::aes(x=group, y=decayrate, color=group)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Decay rate constant k (/s)") +
  ggplot2::ylim(0, 105) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(EMM_k, 
                             label="p = {scales::pvalue(p.value)}", 
                             size=3, step.increase=0.1)

The Models
A t-test would likely be fine here but, because a t-test is just a special case of a linear model, for consistency we again use linear models for amplitude and decay rate as dependent variables, with ligand as the independent factor, checking fit in Figure 1.

# Check model fit

(b) decayrate ~ ligand

title: Supplementary Online Information for Cooper et al. (2026)
text:
This site provides supplementary information to help enable reproduction and independent exploration of the statistical analyses reported in Cooper et al. (2026).
The pages in the Analyses section describe regression modelling for the manuscript “Structural and functional basis of lipid-associated, electrogenic ammonium transport by the Rhesus-family protein NeRh50 in Nitrosomonas europaea” by Cooper et al. We analyse this data to establish evidence in support of answers to the following key questions:

Do maximum amplitude and/or decay rate constant vary for WT NeRh50 in response to changes in lipid-protein ratio (LPR)?
Do maximum amplitude and/or decay rate constant vary for WT NeRh50 in response to a change in substrate from NH4+ to MeA?
Do maximum amplitude and/or decay rate constant vary for WT NeRh50 in response to a changes in pH conditions?
